newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Fourteen killed in fighting in eastern Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Fourteen killed in fighting in eastern Colombia.

text.p: Seven soldiers and eight leftist rebels were killed in heavy fighting in a jungle-covered area of Colombia's eastern Meta province, military spokesmen said on Friday.

They said the fighting, the worst since guerrillas launched a nationwide offensive in September, occurred late on Thursday in the municipality of La Uribe, a stronghold of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).

The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla group, maintained its general headquarters in La Uribe, 105 miles (170 km) southeast of Bogota, until December 1990 when the army launched a major counterinsurgency campaign in the area.

Gen. Rodolfo Herrera, commander of the 7th Army Brigade, said troops backed by helicopter gunships continued their sweep through La Uribe on Friday and the death toll from fighting there could rise by the weekend.
In addition to the seven soldiers killed in la Uribe, military spokesmen said a marine died in a rebel attack on a river patrol boat on Thursday in northern Bolivar province.

President Ernesto Samper appealed on Thursday night for the speedy release of 60 soliders held prisoner by the FARC since Aug. 30 when its forces overran a remote military base in southwestern Putumayo province.
In remarks to reporters, Samper also vowed that there would be no attempt to rescue the innocent soldiers through a covert military operation that could endanger their lives.
